title_en: Xu Shuiyun v. People's Government of Wucheng District, Jinhua City — dispute over administrative compulsory enforcement of housing and administrative compensation
ruling_gist_en: 1. In the process of expropriating houses on state-owned land, only the people's government at the city or county level and the housing expropriation department designated by it have the administrative authority to organize and implement the forced demolition of the lawful houses of the expropriated persons. If the people's government at the city or county level and the housing expropriation department cannot produce evidence to prove that the lawful houses of the expropriated persons were demolished by another entity, they may be identified as the responsible主体 for the forced demolition. Where the people's government at the city or county level and the housing expropriation department entrust a civil subject such as a construction unit to implement the forced demolition, they shall bear legal liability for the consequences of the forced demolition. If a civil subject such as a construction unit carries out an illegal forced demolition in its own name, thereby infringing upon property rights, it shall not only bear civil liability, but also bear administrative liability in accordance with the law if it violates administrative regulations, and shall bear criminal liability in accordance with the law if the act constitutes a crime.

full_text_en:
Xu Shuiyun v. People's Government of Wucheng District, Jinhua City

— Dispute over Administrative Compulsory Demolition of House and Administrative Compensation

Ruling Summary

I. In the process of house expropriation on State-owned land, only the people's government at the city or county level and the house expropriation department designated by it have the administrative authority to organize and implement the compulsory demolition of the lawful houses of the expropriated parties. Where the people's government at the city or county level and the house expropriation department cannot produce evidence to prove that the lawful houses of the expropriated parties were demolished by other entities, they may be identified as the responsible entities for the compulsory demolition. Where the people's government at the city or county level and the house expropriation department entrust construction entities or other civil entities to implement compulsory demolition, the people's government at the city or county level and the house expropriation department shall bear legal liability for the consequences of the compulsory demolition. Where construction entities or other civil entities, in their own names, illegally demolish houses in violation of the law, thereby infringing upon property rights, they shall not only bear civil liability but also bear administrative liability in accordance with the law if they violate administrative regulations, and shall be subject to criminal liability in accordance with the law if the act constitutes a crime.

II. Where a people's government at the city or county level, having neither made a compensation decision nor resolved the compensation issue through a compensation agreement, illegally demolishes the house of an expropriated party by force, it shall compensate the expropriated party for the loss of the house's value, the loss of items inside the house, and losses such as resettlement compensation. When determining the amount of compensation, the people's court shall adhere to the principle of full compensation, reasonably determine the time point for the appraisal of the house and other matters, and comprehensively coordinate the application of the compensation methods, compensation items, and compensation standards provided for in the State Compensation Law and the compensation methods, compensation items, and compensation standards provided for in the Regulations on the Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Their Compensation, so as to ensure that the compensation received by the expropriated party is not less than the expropriation compensation he would have obtained had the expropriation compensation scheme been followed.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Supreme People's Court Admin Re-Trial No. 101

Re-trial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xu Shuiyun, male, born on September 23, 1954, Han nationality, residing at Room 101, Building 368, No. 32 Gongdian Lane, Erqi Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Jinfeng, female, born on December 28, 1955, Han nationality, residing at the same address, spouse of the re-trial applicant Xu Shuiyun.

Agent ad litem: Yang Zaiming, lawyer of Beijing Zaiming Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): People's Government of Wucheng District, Jinhua City. Domicile: No. 2666 Binxi West Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Guo Huiqiang, District Mayor.

Agent ad litem: Wu Jiansun, Deputy Commander of the Erqi Block Reconstruction Project Headquarters, Wucheng District, Jinhua City.

Agent ad litem: Lu Yifeng, lawyer of Zhejiang Fengchang Law Firm.

In the case of the re-trial applicant Xu Shuiyun v. the respondent, the People's Government of Wucheng District, Jinhua City (hereinafter referred to as the Wucheng District Government), concerning administrative compulsory demolition of a house and administrative compensation, the Intermediate People's Court of Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, rendered on December 27, 2016, the Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu Zi No. 19, confirming that the administrative act of the Wucheng District Government in forcibly demolishing Xu Shuiyun's houses located at No. 8 and No. 9 Yingbin Lane, Wuyi Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City, was illegal, and ordering the Wucheng District Government to make compensation to Xu Shuiyun by reference to the Compensation Scheme for House Expropriation for the Old City Reconstruction of the Erqi Block, Wucheng District (hereinafter referred to as the Expropriation Compensation Scheme) within 60 days from the date when the judgment became effective. After Xu Shuiyun appealed, the High People's Court of Zhejiang Province rendered on May 2, 2017, the Administrative Judgment (2017) Zhe Xing Zhong No. 154, affirming Item 1 of the Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu Zi No. 19, reversing Item 2 of the Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu Zi No. 19, and dismissing Xu Shuiyun's other claims. Xu Shuiyun, still dissatisfied, applied to this Court for retrial within the statutory period. This Court rendered on December 27, 2017, the Administrative Ruling (2017) Supreme People's Court Admin Retrial Application No. 8183, deciding to bring this case for retrial, and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear this case, which has now been concluded.

The courts of first and second instance found through trial that, on August 31, 2014, the Wucheng District Government published in Jinhua Daily the Announcement of the People's Government of Wucheng District on the Scope of House Expropriation for the Old City Reconstruction of the Erqi Block and published a map of the house expropriation scope, specifying the implementation of reconstruction for the Erqi Block area. On September 26, 2014, the house in question was demolished by the Wucheng District Government. On October 25, 2014, the Wucheng District Government made the Decision of the People's Government of Wucheng District, Jinhua City on the Expropriation of Houses for the Old City Reconstruction and Construction Project of the Yingbin Lane Block (hereinafter referred to as the House Expropriation Decision), stating: For the need of old city reconstruction, it was decided to expropriate houses within the Yingbin Lane Block; the house expropriation department was the Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Bureau of Wucheng District, Jinhua City; the house expropriation implementing entity was the Erqi Block Reconstruction Project Headquarters of Wucheng District, Jinhua City (hereinafter referred to as the Project Headquarters); the signing period was 45 days, and the relocation period was 30 days, with specific start and end dates to be separately announced by the house expropriation department after the selection of the house expropriation appraisal institution; the attachment was the Expropriation Compensation Scheme. On October 26, 2014, the House Expropriation Decision and the Expropriation Compensation Scheme were published in Jinhua Daily. Xu Shuiyun's houses located at No. 8 and No. 9 Yingbin Lane, Wuyi Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City (hereinafter referred to as the houses in question) were included in the scope of this house expropriation.

It was further found that the houses in the Yingbin Lane Block of Wucheng District, Jinhua City, including Xu Shuiyun's houses in question, had been included in the demolition scope in 2001 due to the reconstruction of the west area of Houxi Street in Jinhua City and the reconstruction of the integrated block of "Two Streets". Jinhua City Construction Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhua Development Company) obtained a house demolition permit, which stated a demolition period from July 10, 2001 to August 9, 2001, but the demolition was not actually completed for some reason.

The court of first instance held that, although the houses in question had been included in the demolition scope in 2001, the demolisher Jinhua Development Company had been unable to demolish the houses in question after obtaining the house demolition permit. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Zhejiang Province Urban House Demolition Management Regulations effective at that time, a house demolition permit naturally expired if the demolisher did not commence demolition within three months from the date of obtaining the permit. Accordingly, it could be confirmed that the houses in question could no longer be demolished in accordance with the regulations and policies formulated for the demolition of houses in the Yingbin Lane Block of Wucheng District, Jinhua City in 2001. After the Wucheng District Government included the houses in question in the expropriation scope through the House Expropriation Decision published on October 26, 2014, it should proceed with expropriation and provide compensation in accordance with the Regulations on the Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Their Compensation (hereinafter referred to as the Expropriation and Compensation Regulations) and other relevant laws and regulations. The Expropriation and Compensation Regulations clearly stipulate that the implementation of house expropriation shall follow the principle of "compensation first, relocation later." If the house expropriation department and the expropriated party fail to reach a compensation agreement within the signing period specified in the expropriation compensation scheme, the house expropriation department shall report to the people's government at the city or county level that made the house expropriation decision to make a compensation decision in accordance with the regulations, based on the expropriation compensation scheme. If the expropriated party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor institutes administrative proceedings within the statutory period, and does not relocate within the period specified in the compensation decision, the people's government at the city or county level that made the house expropriation decision shall apply to the people's court for enforcement in accordance with the law. Xu Shuiyun did not reach a compensation agreement with the house expropriation department, nor did he clearly agree to vacate and deliver the houses in question for demolition. Under such circumstances, the Wucheng District Government should, after making a compensation decision for Xu Shuiyun, proceed with enforcement by applying to the people's court for enforcement, rather than directly demolishing the houses in question. The Wucheng District Government's claim that the houses in question were demolished by a third party lacked sufficient evidence and was inconsistent with the facts found; therefore, its claim was not adopted. The act of demolishing the houses in question by the Wucheng District Government should be confirmed as illegal, and it should bear liability for compensating Xu Shuiyun for the losses suffered as a result. Given that the houses in question had been included in the old city reconstruction scope of the Yingbin Lane Block of Wucheng District, Jinhua City, and there was no possibility or necessity for restoring the houses to their original condition, from the perspective of safeguarding Xu Shuiyun's lawful rights and interests, it was appropriate for the Wucheng District Government to make compensation to Xu Shuiyun by reference to the Expropriation Compensation Scheme. Therefore, the court of first instance, pursuant to Article 74, Paragraph 2, Item 1 and Article 76 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law), rendered the judgment: 1. Confirming that the administrative act of the Wucheng District Government in forcibly demolishing Xu Shuiyun's houses located at No. 8 and No. 9 Yingbin Lane, Wuyi Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City, was illegal; 2. Ordering the Wucheng District Government to make compensation to Xu Shuiyun by reference to the Expropriation Compensation Scheme within 60 days from the date when the judgment became effective.

The court of second instance held that, in July 2001, due to the need for the reconstruction of the west area of Houxi Street in Jinhua City and the reconstruction of the integrated block of "Two Streets," the former Jinhua City Real Estate Administration Bureau issued the House Demolition Permit No. (2001) 3 to Jinhua Development Company, and the houses in question were included in the demolition red line scope of the said demolition permit, but the demolisher failed to carry out demolition within the period specified in the demolition permit. Point 9 of the minutes of the meeting of the Jinhua City Old City Reconstruction Office formed on August 20, 2004 (Jin Old City Office [2004] No. 1) recorded: Regarding the unresolved issues of the expropriated households of Yingbin Lane, Yingbin Lane No. 1-48, and others, including the old houses not yet demolished, the meeting agreed that these issues should be resolved together when the demolition of the "Erqi" New Village is carried out, with the demolition work to be handled by the original demolition company. On October 26, 2014, the Wucheng District Government published the House Expropriation Decision, including the houses in question in the expropriation scope, but the houses were demolished on September 26, 2014, before the publication of the House Expropriation Decision, which violated the principle of "compensation first, relocation later" as stipulated in Article 27 of the Expropriation and Compensation Regulations. The legal liability for the act of demolishing the houses in question should be borne by the Wucheng District Government, which made the House Expropriation Decision. The Wucheng District Government's argument that "it did not carry out the forced demolition of the house, and the damage to the houses in question was caused by a third party, which constitutes a civil tort compensation dispute, not an administrative dispute, and is unrelated to it" lacked factual and legal basis. The court of first instance's judgment confirming the illegality of the Wucheng District Government's forced demolition act was not erroneous. Article 4 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the State Compensation Law) provides that where an administrative organ or its personnel causes property damage in the exercise of administrative powers, the injured party has the right to obtain compensation. Article 32, Paragraph 2 provides that if the property can be returned or the original condition restored, the property shall be returned or the original condition restored. Xu Shuiyun's houses had been included in the expropriation scope by the House Expropriation Decision. Although the expropriation decision in question had been confirmed illegal by the effective Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Xing Zhong No. 74, it had not been revoked, and the expropriation decision and its annex remained effective. Therefore, Xu Shuiyun's request for restoration of original condition could not be sustained. At the second instance, Xu Shuiyun requested that, if restoration was not possible, he be compensated based on the market price of surrounding real estate. Although the houses in question were illegally demolished by the Wucheng District Government, the related rights and interests that Xu Shuiyun should have obtained through expropriation could still be compensated through the expropriation compensation procedures. Xu Shuiyun's claim to resolve the loss from the illegal demolition of the houses in question through the state compensation procedures lacked corresponding legal basis. Similarly, the court of first instance's direct order for the Wucheng District Government to make compensation to Xu Shuiyun by reference to the Expropriation Compensation Scheme also lacked legal basis and could potentially deprive Xu Shuiyun of the right to remedy for compensation and resettlement of the houses in question. Additionally, Xu Shuiyun's claim for compensation for losses from cessation of business and production at RMB 20,000 per month (until the date of restoration of the house to its original condition) fell within the scope of house expropriation compensation and could be resolved through the expropriation compensation procedures. As for Xu Shuiyun's claim for compensation for property losses of RMB 60,000, since he did not provide evidence of the relevant property losses, it was not supported. Therefore, the court of second instance, pursuant to Article 89, Paragraph 1, Items 1 and 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law, rendered the judgment: 1. Affirming Item 1 of the Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu Zi No. 19 of the Intermediate People's Court of Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province; 2. Reversing Item 2 of the Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu Zi No. 19 of the Intermediate People's Court of Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province; 3. Dismissing Xu Shuiyun's other claims.

Xu Shuiyun applied to this Court for retrial, requesting the reversal of Items 2 and 3 of the Administrative Judgment (2017) Zhe Xing Zhong No. 154 of the High People's Court of Zhejiang Province, and the amendment of the judgment to order the Wucheng District Government to restore the houses in question to their original condition, or if restoration is not possible, to order the Wucheng District Government to compensate him based on the market price of surrounding real estate, and also to order the Wucheng District Government to compensate for losses from cessation of business and production at RMB 20,000 per month and property losses such as items inside the house totaling RMB 60,000. The main facts and reasons for his retrial application were: 1. The judgment of the court of second instance failed to correctly distinguish the fundamental difference between administrative compensation and administrative expropriation compensation, and considered that the compensation issue could be resolved through expropriation compensation procedures, which constituted insufficient evidence and an error in finding facts. 2. The judgment of the court of second instance dismissed the re-trial applicant's compensation claim and required the re-trial applicant to separately resolve it through expropriation compensation procedures, which lacked legal basis and was not conducive to protecting the re-trial applicant's lawful rights and interests. 3. The respondent, the Wucheng District Government, should bear administrative compensation liability for the loss of items caused to the re-trial applicant by the illegal forced demolition. 4. The judgment of the court of second instance allowed the respondent, the Wucheng District Government, to avoid legal liability for its illegal act, which would deprive the re-trial applicant of the right to judicial remedy for the economic losses arising therefrom. In summary, the re-trial applicant believed that the respondent, the Wucheng District Government, should bear the legal liability for restoring the houses in question to their original condition or compensating based on market prices for the illegal demolition.

The Wucheng District Government argued in its defense that it respected the court's judgment. 1. The houses in question were old houses formed historically, and as a legacy issue from demolition, the respondent agreed to compensate them as lawful buildings. 2. The respondent did not organize personnel to forcibly demolish the houses in question. Because the houses in question were old and located adjacent to other houses to be demolished, the Project Headquarters entrusted Wucheng District Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wucheng Construction Company) to demolish the houses of third parties who had reached compensation and resettlement agreements. Due to improper construction, the houses in question collapsed. This was a civil dispute arising from the civil tort of Wucheng Construction Company, and the respondent should not bear legal liability for it. 3. The houses in question could not be compensated as commercial premises. 4. The respondent had repeatedly negotiated with the re-trial applicant Xu Shuiyun on multiple occasions and was also willing to make lawful and reasonable compensation to protect his lawful rights and interests, hoping that the re-trial applicant Xu Shuiyun would understand and cooperate.

This Court holds that the main issues in dispute in this case include four aspects: I. The identification of the entity responsible for the forced demolition; II. Whether the demolition act in this case was illegal; III. Whether this case should be remedied through administrative compensation or administrative expropriation compensation procedures; IV. The determination of the method, items, standards, and amount of compensation.

I. Identification of the entity responsible for the forced demolition

Article 4, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Expropriation and Compensation Regulations provide that the people's government at the city or county level shall be responsible for the house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. The house expropriation department designated by the people's government at the city or county level shall organize and implement the house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. Article 5 provides that the house expropriation department may entrust a house expropriation implementing entity to carry out the specific work of house expropriation and compensation. The house expropriation implementing entity shall not operate for profit. The house expropriation department shall supervise the house expropriation and compensation acts carried out by the house expropriation implementing entity within the scope of the entrustment and shall bear legal liability for the consequences of such acts. Article 28, Paragraph 1 provides that if the expropriated party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor institutes administrative proceedings within the statutory period, and does not relocate within the period specified in the compensation decision, the people's government at the city or county level that made the house expropriation decision shall apply to the people's court for enforcement in accordance with the law. According to the above provisions, in the process of house expropriation on State-owned land, only the people's government at the city or county level and the house expropriation department designated by it have the authority to lawfully forcibly demolish lawful buildings. Civil entities such as construction entities and construction units do not have the power to forcibly demolish others' lawful houses. If a civil entity illegally forcibly demolishes another's lawful house on its own, which may constitute the crime of intentional destruction of property, the right holder may request the public security organ to perform its duties in accordance with the law; if the people's court, upon review, finds that a criminal act exists, it shall transfer the relevant materials to the public security or procuratorial organs pursuant to Article 66, Paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law. Therefore, unless the people's government at the city or county level can prove that the house was indeed forcibly demolished by a relevant civil entity without its knowledge, it shall be presumed that the forced demolition was carried out on entrustment by the people's government at the city or county level, and the people's court may identify the people's government at the city or county level as the administrative entity that implemented the forced demolition, and it shall bear corresponding compensation liability.

In this case, the Wucheng District Government claimed that on September 26, 2014, when the Project Headquarters entrusted Wucheng Construction Company to demolish the houses of third parties who had reached compensation and resettlement agreements, the houses in question collapsed due to improper operation; the statement issued by Wucheng Construction Company on March 6, 2015 also contained similar representations. Based on this, the Wucheng District Government denied that the forced demolition was organized and implemented by the government, arguing that the damage to the houses in question was caused by the third party, Wucheng Construction Company, and that this constituted a civil tort compensation dispute unrelated to the Wucheng District Government and not an administrative dispute. However, the forced demolition of the houses in question occurred during the expropriation process where the Wucheng District Government was the expropriation entity. Before the houses in question were demolished, on August 31, 2014, the Wucheng District Government published the announcement of house expropriation for old city reconstruction, including the houses in question in the expropriation scope. Therefore, for the act of forcibly demolishing lawful houses occurring during the house expropriation process, it should first be presumed to be an administrative coercive act implemented by the Wucheng District Government and its designated house expropriation department, and they shall bear corresponding responsibility. Although Wucheng Construction Company voluntarily admitted to "demolishing by mistake" in this case, the text message sent by the staff of the Project Headquarters to Xu Shuiyun recorded content such as "I am a staff member of the Erqi New Village Block Reconstruction Project Headquarters of Wucheng District, Jinhua City, and we will carry out a notarized inspection of the house; if you do not cooperate, we will break in to conduct a safety inspection and notarization," and the photos of the demolition site provided by Xu Shuiyun showing administrative law enforcement personnel present, as well as relevant local news reports, all confirmed that the forced demolition on September 26, 2014, was carried out under the leadership of the government. Therefore, the Wucheng District Government's argument that the forced demolition was a civil tort could not be sustained. The legal liability for Wucheng Construction Company's act of demolishing the houses in question should be borne by the Project Headquarters that entrusted it with the demolition; the Project Headquarters was a temporary institution established by the Wucheng District Government and endowed with administrative functions but lacking the capacity to independently bear legal liability. Therefore, the Wucheng District Government should be the defendant and bear corresponding legal liability.

II. Whether the demolition act in this case was illegal

Article 4 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the property rights of the State, collectives, individuals and other right holders are protected by law and may not be infringed upon by any entity or individual. Paragraph 1 of Article 42 provides that for the needs of the public interest, land owned by collectives and houses and other immovable property owned by entities and individuals may be expropriated in accordance with the authority and procedures prescribed by law; Paragraph 3 provides that when expropriating houses and other immovable property of entities and individuals, demolition compensation shall be given according to law, and the legitimate rights and interests of the expropriated persons shall be protected; when expropriating individual residential houses, the living conditions of the expropriated persons shall also be guaranteed.

Xu Shuiyun's houses located at No. 8 and No. 9, Yingbin Lane, Wucheng District, Jinhua City did not undergo relevant construction procedures according to law and did not obtain house ownership certificates, but the houses in question were indeed historically old houses built before the implementation of the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China on April 1, 1990. For such unregistered houses, investigation, determination and treatment shall be conducted according to law, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the construction history, current use status, local land use planning, and relevant land use policies. For buildings determined to be legal and temporary buildings that have not exceeded the approved period, compensation shall be given. Based on the payment receipts for land registration fees and house registration fees paid by Xu Baoxian and Shou Jiming, as well as the application form for registration of private house ownership submitted by Shou Jiming and other materials provided by Xu Shuiyun, the Reconstruction Project Headquarters and the court of first instance have determined that the houses in question are legal buildings. Xu Shuiyun became the owner of the houses through inheritance and purchase, and owns ownership of the houses in question, which no entity or individual may infringe upon. If the State needs to expropriate for the public interest, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, give fair compensation to the house owner, and implement relocation only after compensation has been given first, in accordance with Article 27 of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation. The house owner also has the obligation and responsibility to actively cooperate with and support the house expropriation after signing the compensation agreement or receiving the compensation content determined by the compensation decision. The Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Applications for Enforcement by the People's Courts of Compensation Decisions on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land systematically and strictly regulate how city and county people's governments and house expropriation departments implement expropriation, how to compensate, how to enforce relocation, and how to ensure that the expropriated persons obtain fair compensation based on market assessment prices. At the same time, to ensure the smooth and efficient implementation of house expropriation for public interest needs, it is specifically provided that compulsory relocation may be carried out according to law for the very few expropriated persons who do not perform the compensation decision and do not voluntarily relocate. Specifically in this case, in accordance with the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, the Wucheng District Government should first make a house expropriation decision and announce it, then conclude a compensation agreement with Xu Shuiyun on matters such as the compensation method, compensation amount, and payment period; if the parties cannot reach a compensation agreement within the signing period determined by the expropriation compensation plan, the city or county people's government shall then unilaterally make a compensation decision according to law. If the expropriated person is dissatisfied with the compensation decision, they may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law, or may initiate an administrative lawsuit according to law; if the expropriated person does not apply for administrative reconsideration or initiate an administrative lawsuit within the statutory period, and does not relocate within the period specified in the compensation decision, the city or county people's government that made the house expropriation decision shall apply to the people's court for compulsory enforcement according to law. After the people's court rules to permit enforcement, it is generally implemented by the city or county people's government that made the expropriation compensation decision, or may be enforced by the people's court. This is the legal procedure that a lawful expropriation and compensation should follow, and it is also the basic requirement of the law for expropriation and compensation. This Court notes that the expropriation and demolition of the houses in question began as early as July 2001 when Jinhua Development Company obtained the demolition permit. Over a period of more than ten years, if the failure to sign a compensation and resettlement agreement was due to the house owner making illegal compensation requests, the Wucheng District Government and its functional departments should have exercised the administrative powers granted by laws and regulations according to law, promptly made a demolition resettlement ruling or compensation decision, given Xu Shuiyun fair compensation, and promptly enforced compulsory relocation to ensure the realization of the public interest and the smooth progress of the demolition and expropriation work. However, the Wucheng District Government and the corresponding functional departments neither performed their duties promptly according to law, nor protected the legitimate rights and interests of the expropriated person, nor correctly understood the legislative purpose of the compulsory relocation system under the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, nor achieved the smooth implementation of the old city reconstruction project; instead, they delayed for a long time and illegally demolished the expropriated person's house by means of a so-called civil "mistaken demolition", ultimately having to bear compensation liability. The judgments of the courts of first and second instance confirming that the forced demolition act of the Wucheng District Government was illegal are in accordance with legal provisions, and this Court supports them.

III. Regarding the issue of whether relief should be sought through administrative compensation or administrative expropriation compensation procedures

Administrative compensation refers to the system where the State compensates according to law for losses caused to the legitimate rights and interests of administrative counterparts by administrative organs implementing lawful administrative acts. Administrative damages refers to the system where the State compensates according to law for losses caused to the legitimate rights and interests of administrative counterparts by administrative organs implementing unlawful administrative acts. In the process of expropriating houses on state-owned land, the issue of compensation for losses caused by unlawful expropriation and expropriation-related administrative acts is relatively complex. This includes, among other things, compensation for losses to the property rights of the right holder caused by unlawful demolition, compensation for losses of benefits that should have been compensated due to failure to carry out expropriation compensation in accordance with Article 17 of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation and local expropriation compensation policies, and even losses from relocation, temporary resettlement, and subsidies and incentives that should have been given. Especially in administrative compensation lawsuits filed together with forced demolition, the people's court shall, in light of the type and severity of the unlawful act, comprehensively and coordinately apply the compensation methods, items, and standards provided in the State Compensation Law and the compensation methods, items, and standards provided in the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, to determine the compensation items and amounts according to law and scientifically, so that the compensation received by the expropriated person is not lower than the expropriation compensation they could have received under the expropriation compensation plan, ensuring that the property owner receives fair and reasonable compensation. At the same time, when determining the compensation obligor and the amount of compensation, the people's court must adhere to the legal concepts of whoever has power must bear responsibility, illegality must be accountable, infringement must be compensated, and compensation must be comprehensive. For administrative organs that illegally forcibly demolish the house of an expropriated person, infringing on the property rights of the house owner, the administrative organ shall be ordered to bear administrative compensation liability according to law, and the property owner shall not receive compensation for the infringement that is lower than the compensation they should have received for lawful expropriation.

Under normal circumstances, the forced demolition of an expropriated person's house should be based on a compensation decision that has already taken effect, and the compensation decision should have already resolved the compensation issue for the house itself. Therefore, even if the forced demolition act is found to be illegal, it usually only involves compensation for damage to items inside the house, and should not involve compensation for the house itself. However, in this case, before the forced demolition, there was neither an expropriation decision nor a compensation decision, Xu Shuiyun did not agree to the prior demolition of the house, and to date the parties have not reached a compensation and resettlement agreement, and Xu Shuiyun has not received any form of compensation. The forced demolition has constituted a major and obvious illegality and shall be compensated according to law. The compensation for Xu Shuiyun's house loss should no longer be determined based on the market price of similar real estate in the expropriated house on the date of announcement of the House Expropriation Decision as stipulated in Article 19 of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, i.e., the market price on October 26, 2014, but should be determined based on the market price of similar real estate in the houses in question at the time the Wucheng District Government makes the compensation decision after this judgment takes effect, in accordance with the principle of fully protecting Xu Shuiyun's house property rights. At the same time, according to Article 36(8) of the State Compensation Law, which provides that for other damages to property rights, compensation shall be given for direct losses, the losses of benefits that Xu Shuiyun should have received according to law and local expropriation compensation policies in the normal expropriation compensation procedure constitute direct losses suffered by him, and shall also be compensated by the Wucheng District Government with reference to the compensation plan according to law. Therefore, in this case, there is a situation where the items and standards of administrative compensation and administrative expropriation compensation are merged. The second item of the first instance judgment ordering the Wucheng District Government to compensate Xu Shuiyun with reference to the Expropriation Compensation Plan; the second instance judgment holding that relief should be obtained through subsequent expropriation compensation procedures and accordingly dismissing Xu Shuiyun's claim for administrative damages, both constitute a misunderstanding of the relevant provisions of the State Compensation Law, the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, etc., and shall be corrected.

IV. Regarding the determination of compensation methods, items, standards, and amounts

Specifically in this case, according to Xu Shuiyun's claims, the losses he asserts include the following three parts: first, loss of the house; second, loss of cessation of production and business; third, loss of items inside the house. The Wucheng District Government and Xu Shuiyun shall negotiate on an equal footing regarding the above three losses, and may resolve the matter by signing a settlement agreement; if the parties cannot reach an agreement, the Wucheng District Government shall promptly make an administrative compensation decision in accordance with the method determined in this judgment.

(1) Issues concerning the method and standard of compensation for house loss

Article 32 of the State Compensation Law provides that State compensation is mainly in the form of payment of compensation money. If the property can be returned or restored to its original state, it shall be returned or restored to its original state. Accordingly, returning property or restoring the original state is the preferred method of State compensation, which meets the requirements of the claimant and is more convenient and quicker; however, its applicable condition is that the original object has not been disposed of or damaged or lost. If the relevant property can no longer be returned or restored to its original state, corresponding compensation money shall be paid or other compensation methods shall be adopted. In this case, the house in question has already been included in the expropriation scope of the old city reconstruction and has been demolished by the Wucheng District Government. Therefore, this Court does not support Xu Shuiyun's claim for restoration of the original state of the house. The house in question was demolished due to old city reconstruction. If it were a lawful expropriation and demolition, Xu Shuiyun could either choose monetary compensation based on the market assessment price on the date of announcement of the expropriation decision, or have the right to choose similar houses in the reconstruction area or nearby areas for property rights exchange. This case involves compensation arising from unlawful forced demolition. Article 4(3) of the State Compensation Law provides that if an administrative organ unlawfully expropriates, infringing on property rights, the victim has the right to obtain compensation. Therefore, to reflect the punishment for unlawful expropriation and unlawful demolition acts and effectively protect Xu Shuiyun's legitimate rights and interests, the compensation for Xu Shuiyun's house shall not be lower than the compensation he should have received for lawful expropriation. That is, the compensation for Xu Shuiyun's house shall not be lower than the market value of similar houses in the reconstruction area or nearby areas at the time of compensation. Considering the provisions of Article 36 of the State Compensation Law and Xu Shuiyun's request for retrial, the Wucheng District Government may compensate either by providing similar houses in the reconstruction area or nearby areas, or by paying compensation based on the effective real estate market assessment price at the time of making the compensation decision. The Wucheng District Government and Xu Shuiyun may determine the real estate price assessment institution in accordance with the method prescribed in Article 20 of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation. Given that the house in question has been demolished, the real estate assessment institution may, with reference to the method prescribed in Article 13 of the Measures for the Assessment of House Expropriation on State-owned Land, based on the original materials provided by the Wucheng District Government and Xu Shuiyun, and in the spirit of resolving doubts in favor of the property owner, independently, objectively, and fairly issue an assessment report.

(2) Issues concerning the standard of compensation for losses from cessation of production and business

In this case, Xu Shuiyun claimed that because the house was demolished, his business was ceased, and he demanded compensation for losses from cessation of production and business up to the present at RMB 20,000 per month. The Wucheng District Government acknowledged the fact that Xu Shuiyun engaged in business activities, but argued that because Xu Shuiyun's house was an unlicensed building, it could only be compensated as ordinary housing, and no compensation for cessation of production and business losses should be calculated. This Court holds that Article 23 of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation provides that compensation for losses from cessation of production and business caused by house expropriation shall be determined based on factors such as the benefits before the house was expropriated and the period of cessation of production and business. Specific measures shall be formulated by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government. Article 29(1) of the Regulations of Zhejiang Province on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation provides that for losses from cessation of production and business caused by expropriation of non-residential houses, compensation shall be given based on factors such as the benefits before the house was expropriated and the period of cessation of production and business. The compensation standard shall not be lower than five percent of the value of the expropriated house, and the specific standard shall be prescribed by the people's government of the city divided into districts or the county (city). Article 34(1) of the Implementation Opinions on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation in Jinhua Urban Area (for Trial Implementation) provides that for losses from cessation of production and business caused by expropriation of non-residential houses, compensation shall be calculated at five percent of the value of the expropriated house.

Article 24(2) of the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation provides that before making a house expropriation decision, a city or county people's government shall organize relevant departments to investigate, determine, and deal with unregistered buildings within the expropriation scope according to law. For buildings determined to be legal and temporary buildings that have not exceeded the approved period, compensation shall be given; for buildings determined to be illegal and temporary buildings that have exceeded the approved period, no compensation shall be given. Since the houses in question have been determined to be legal buildings, they have the same legal status as houses with house ownership certificates in terms of compensation. If the evidence provided by Xu Shuiyun, such as business licenses and tax payment certificates, can prove that his houses meet the conditions for business premises (non-residential houses) as determined by the Regulations on Expropriation and Compensation, the Regulations of Zhejiang Province on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation, and the Implementation Opinions on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation in Jinhua Urban Area (for Trial Implementation), then the Wucheng District Government shall reasonably determine the amount of losses from cessation of production and business and compensate accordingly. However, since the loss from cessation of production and business during the expropriation process is only to compensate for temporary operational difficulties caused to the house owner by the expropriation, and has the nature of transitional expenses, it can only be paid for an appropriate period or at an appropriate proportion of the house compensation amount. At the same time, the house owner should also promptly find a suitable location to resume business within an appropriate period after the expropriation or infringing act occurs, and cannot shift all losses from not operating due to its own reasons onto the administrative organ. Therefore, Xu Shuiyun's request for retrial, claiming compensation for monthly cessation of production and business losses of RMB 20,000 until the house is restored to its original state, has no legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

(3) Issues concerning the method of determining the amount of compensation for losses of items inside the house

Article 15(1) of the State Compensation Law provides that when a people's court hears an administrative compensation case, the claimant and the compensation obligor shall provide evidence for the claims they put forward. Article 27(3) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China further provides that in an administrative compensation lawsuit filed together, the plaintiff shall bear the burden of proof for the fact of damage caused by the alleged act. Article 5 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation also provides that in an administrative compensation lawsuit, the plaintiff shall provide evidence for the fact of damage caused by the alleged specific administrative act. Therefore, Xu Shuiyun shall bear the burden of proof for the fact, extent, and amount of loss of items inside his house; otherwise, he will bear adverse consequences. At the same time, Article 38(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law also provides that in administrative compensation cases, the plaintiff shall provide evidence for the damage caused by the administrative act. If the plaintiff is unable to provide evidence due to the defendant's reasons, the defendant shall bear the burden of proof. Therefore, if the administrative organ, in violation of due process, fails to notarize or produce a list of evidence according to law, causing difficulties for the plaintiff in fulfilling the burden of proof, and the defendant is also unable to prove the actual amount of loss, the people's court may, when the plaintiff provides evidence that can preliminarily prove its claim regarding the amount of loss, make a determination of the amount of loss unfavorable to the administrative organ according to law. Based on the relevant photos and lists provided by Xu Shuiyun to the court of first instance, it can be determined that there were items such as bird cages in the house in question, which is consistent with the situation of his actual operation of a flower and bird business. Under the circumstance that Xu Shuiyun has preliminarily proven the existence of losses, his reasonable and fair compensation claims should be supported. The Wucheng District Government may, based on market conditions, combined with the actual business situation of Xu Shuiyun and the provided on-site photos and item loss lists, determine the compensation amount at its discretion in accordance with the principle of favoring Xu Shuiyun, and compensate for the loss of property inside the house according to law.

In summary, the basic facts determined by the judgments of the courts of first and second instance are clear. The judgment of the courts of first and second instance confirming that the administrative act of the Wucheng District Government forcibly demolishing Xu Shuiyun's house was illegal is correct, and this Court affirms it. However, the first instance judgment ordering the Wucheng District Government to compensate Xu Shuiyun with reference to the Expropriation Compensation Plan failed to consider that the market price of similar real estate at the time of making the compensation decision had risen significantly compared to the market price of similar real estate at the time of compensation determined in the Expropriation Compensation Plan. Compensating only with reference to the Expropriation Compensation Plan cannot support Xu Shuiyun's claim for compensation for the house. The second instance judgment, which held that the compensation issue in this case should be resolved through the expropriation compensation procedure, failed to consider that the house in question was not expropriated and forcibly relocated according to legal procedures, but was illegally forcibly demolished, and the Wucheng District Government should bear compensation liability. The second item of the first instance judgment and the second and third items of the second instance judgment all constitute errors in the application of law and shall be corrected. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 89(1)(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 76(1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The first item of Administrative Judgment (2017) Zhe Xing Zhong No. 154 of the Zhejiang High People's Court and the first item of Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu No. 19 of the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, are affirmed, i.e., the administrative act of the Wucheng District People's Government of Jinhua City forcibly demolishing Xu Shuiyun's houses located at No. 8 and No. 9, Yingbin Lane, Wuyi Road, Wucheng District, Jinhua City is confirmed to be unlawful.

2. The second and third items of Administrative Judgment (2017) Zhe Xing Zhong No. 154 of the Zhejiang High People's Court and the second item of Administrative Judgment (2015) Zhe Jin Xing Chu No. 19 of the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, are vacated.

3. The Wucheng District People's Government of Jinhua City is ordered to provide administrative compensation to Xu Shuiyun according to law within ninety days from the date this judgment takes effect, in accordance with this judgment.

The total case acceptance fee for the first and second instances is RMB 100, to be borne by the respondent, the Wucheng District People's Government of Jinhua City.

This judgment is final.
